text:
maria: Heads-up — customer wants a fully offline, closed-source inference bundle for Cormac-7B (model + runtime) to run in their air-gapped datacenter. Can we legally ship a binary-only container that includes quantized weights?

jason-mlops: short answer: depends on the model license. which asset did we pull? link to the repo/weights?

maria: grabbed weights from hf://cormac-7b-v1 (the release page links a license file). They specifically asked for: a docker image with our optimized runtime + quantized weights, and an install script. No source code for the runtime to be provided to customer.

oliver-research: on the ML side, quantization itself doesn't usually change copyright status, but redistributing the weight file (even quantized) can fall under redistribution/derivative clauses. also need to check attribution and notice requirements.

sara-legal: I skimmed the license in that repo. It has a clause that forbids "redistribution in binary form in a closed-source product" and requires preserving NOTICE and attribution in all redistributions. That suggests we can't deliver a black-box image without meeting those obligations.

maria: if we can't give a closed binary, options: (1) offer them a hosted Dedicated instance (we keep weights), (2) provide a container but include the NOTICE and license text in the image and deliver the runtime source, or (3) negotiate a commercial sublicense with the model authors. thoughts?

rahul: option 1 is easiest technically and preserves compliance. but the customer explicitly needs on-prem air-gapped deployment for compliance reasons.

jason-mlops: option 2 is doable — we can add /LICENSE and /NOTICE in image and make runtime source tarball available. customer still gets an image but with required attributions and source code. do we need to include source for model weights? they usually don't require model training code, just license text and any required attribution statements.

sara-legal: precisely: the model license requires including the license and NOTICE and making any modifications explicit. If we modify weights (quantize or prune), that might be treated as a derivative. So we need a record of changes and the license's derivative-handling rules. If the license is copyleft-ish it could force source disclosure of modifications — consult upstream.

oliver-research: we do quantize in a deterministic way with our toolchain. can document the steps and include a checksum and diff notes. that should satisfy a lot of attribution/derivative tracking needs, but won't avoid an express copyleft requirement to distribute source if present.

maria: action items: Sara, can you confirm whether this specific license triggers copyleft-for-derivatives or only attribution?

sara-legal: will do. also flagging export control: shipping model weights internationally may require export screening depending on the jurisdiction. I'll coordinate with compliance.

jason-mlops: tech follow-ups for packaging: if we're allowed to distribute an image, add /usr/share/doc/CORMAC_LICENSE.txt and /usr/share/doc/CORMAC_NOTICE.txt, and a /opt/cormac/CHANGES_QUANTIZATION.md with the quant steps + seed + tool versions. sample docker note:
```
FROM redwood/inference-runtime:stable
COPY cormac-7b-qweights/ /opt/models/cormac-7b/
COPY CORMAC_LICENSE.txt /usr/share/doc/
COPY CORMAC_NOTICE.txt /usr/share/doc/
COPY CHANGES_QUANTIZATION.md /opt/models/cormac-7b/
```

rahul: also add an automated checklist in the release pipeline that records the upstream license hash we reviewed and the legal sign-off id. saves us from repeating this later.

sara-legal: agreed. I'll try to get a definitive interpretation by EOD. If the license is strictly non-redistributable in binaries, we'll need to either (a) broker a sublicense or (b) deliver source and attribution per terms.

maria: great. i'll pause the image build until legal confirms. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
